1.title: Custom Conditions: Validation, Preconditions, Postconditions and Checks
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Custom Conditions: Validation, Preconditions, Postconditions and Checks. It covers the exam area four. Terraform configuration. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Why custom conditions. Variable validation. Preconditions and postconditions. Check blocks. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: four. Terraform configuration. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Why custom conditions
1.text: Why custom conditions. Custom conditions let you state assumptions and rules in the configuration, so Terraform fails early with a clear message instead of creating wrong infrastructure.

1.title: Why custom conditions, continued
1.text: Why custom conditions. The figure shows this: Four ways to validate: variable validation, precondition, postcondition and check blocks.

1.title: Why custom conditions, continued
1.text: Why custom conditions. Variable validation. Where: Inside a variable block. When it runs: When the input value is evaluated. If it fails: Error: plan stops. Precondition. Where: In the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or directly in an output block. When it runs: Before the object is created or read. If it fails: Error: plan or apply stops. Postcondition. Where: In the same places. When it runs: After the object is created or read. If it fails: Error: plan or apply stops.

1.title: Why custom conditions, continued
1.text: Why custom conditions. Check block. Where: A top-level check block with assert. When it runs: At the end of plan and apply, as a separate step. If it fails: Warning only; does not block.

1.title: Variable validation
1.text: Variable validation. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Variable validation, continued
1.text: Variable validation. condition. An expression that must be true. error message. The text shown when it is false. A variable can have several validation blocks. The condition can only refer to that variable in older versions; from Terraform one point nine it may refer to other objects.

1.title: Preconditions and postconditions
1.text: Preconditions and postconditions. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Preconditions and postconditions, continued
1.text: Preconditions and postconditions. Precondition. Checks: Assumptions before the object is used (inputs, other resources). Can use self?: No. Postcondition. Checks: Guarantees after the object exists (its attributes). Can use self?: Yes, self is the object. Exam tip: Precondition equals before, postcondition equals after (and self is allowed). Both live in a lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or directly in an output block.

1.title: Check blocks
1.text: Check blocks. A check block runs assertions about the real infrastructure and reports problems as warnings, so it never stops a plan or apply. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Check blocks, continued
1.text: Check blocks. Scoped data source. A data block inside the check is only for that check; if it fails, only a warning appears. Purpose. Continuous validation of things like health and certificates. H C P Terraform. Can run checks regularly and report them (Module sixteen). Exam tip: check warns; validation, precondition and postcondition stop. Use check for monitoring, not for protection. Exam tip: Match the tool to the moment: bad input equals validation, assumption about other objects equals precondition, guarantee about the new object equals postcondition, monitoring equals check.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. A team wants Terraform to reject any input value for a variable named environment that is not dev, test or prod. What should they add? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A validation block in the variable. A validation block with a condition and an error message rejects invalid input values.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which custom condition runs before the resource is created and can stop the plan if an assumption is false? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A precondition. A precondition checks assumptions before the object is created or read.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. A team wants to verify an attribute of an image that was just looked up. Which condition fits and can use self? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A postcondition in the lifecycle block. A postcondition runs after the object exists and can refer to its attributes through self.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. Which feature reports a problem as a warning without blocking the run? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A check block with an assert. Check blocks report failed assertions as warnings and never stop the plan or apply.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Where are preconditions and postconditions written? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or in an output block. Both condition types belong to the lifecycle block of a resource or data source, or to an output block.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. What two arguments does a validation block need? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: condition and error message. A validation block has a condition expression and an error message.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Which custom condition runs after the object exists? Answer: A postcondition. Question two. Which custom condition only warns? Answer: A check block. Question three. Where does variable validation live? Answer: Inside the variable block.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Can a postcondition use self? Answer: Yes. Question five. What does error message hold? Answer: The text shown when the condition is false. Question six. What does a failing precondition do? Answer: Stops the plan or apply with an error.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. validation: in the variable block; condition and error message; error. precondition or postcondition: in lifecycle (or an output block); before or after (self allowed); error. check: top-level; assert; warning only; scoped data source.
